advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a relocated-tracker case asserting a close with file_impact but NO referencing commit still fails fast (pre-LLM) when REBAR_TRACKER_DIR points outside the code repo.
evidence: Only test in the new file: test_cli_close_uses_code_repo_when_tracker_is_relocated asserts transition_command.transition_cli(...) == 0, calls == [ticket_id], status closed, certified — all on the PASS path.
The change routes _check_work_landed through code_root: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:635 `_check_work_landed(ticket_id, resolved_id, accepted_ids, tracker, code_root)`.

The true-missing-commit negative control exists only for the default in-repo tracker (tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py:335 test_file_impact_without_referencing_commit_blocks), not for the relocated (REBAR_TRACKER_DIR) case introduced by this fix.
Ticket AC-2 'A true missing referencing commit still fails before the completion LLM call' is asserted only against the default root, not the relocated scenario this diff targets.
advisory.finding: The new relocated-tracker regression test covers only the success path (commit found, verifier runs, close certified); there is no relocated-tracker case asserting that a truly-missing referencing commit still fails-fast before the LLM call, so a regression that scanned the wrong code root (e.g. one that happens to contain an unrelated commit) in the external-tracker scenario would not be caught here.
scenarios: Relocated REBAR_TRACKER_DIR where the fix's code_root resolution regresses to a root that contains some unrelated commit but not the ticket's trailer — close would spuriously proceed and no test would fail.
